-Db 
Chief Justice's Court
Case :- Writ Tax No. - 1025 of 2025

Petitioner :- Vimla Devi and 3 others
Respondent :- State of U.P. and 3 others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Deshraj Garg
Counsel for Respondent :- Nimai Dass, A.C.S.C.
Hon'ble Arun Bhansali,Chief Justice
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.
This petition has been filed by the petitioners seeking a direction to the respondents to refund the amount of TDS, which was deducted from the compensation paid to the petitioners.
2. Submissions have been made that land of the petitioners was acquired for National Highways and compensation was paid to the petitioners.
From the compensation, a sum of Rs. 13,894/- each has been deducted as TDS and Form No. 16A has been issued to the petitioners.

Submissions have been made that the petitioners have moved applications to the Land Acquisition Officer for refund of the said amount and, therefore, the authority may be directed to decide the said representations.
3.

A perusal of the record indicates that the amount deducted as TDS has already been deposited by the Land Acquisition Officer, which is evident from Form No. 16A (Annexure-5), wherein the PAN numbers of the petitioners are also reflected.

sentences.text: In view of the fact that amount already stands deposited with the Income Tax Department, the refund can only be given in terms of the provisions of the Income Tax Act, wherein petitioners are required to file their return and seek refund of the excess amount deducted/deposited.

5. In that view of the matter, the relief claimed in the petition for refund of TDS from respondents and seeking disposal of the writ petition would not come to the aid of the petitioners qua seeking the material relief of getting the refund.
6. In that view of the matter, the petition stands disposed of.
7. The petitioners may take action in accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax Act for seeking refund of the amount of TDS deposited by the competent authority/Land Acquisition Officer.
